newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares squeezed to their third consecutive record high close on Friday, with volume stoked up by the biggest options turnover on record.

Dealers said buying in the cash market to cover options positions, combined with an overnight Wall Street gain and a surging dollar had pushed shares from the outset, although profit-taking late in the afternoon pared back gains.

The AEX closed at 670.08, extending Thursday's 7.88 point gain by a wafer-thin 0.53 points. Earlier business swept the index to an all-time high of 673.36, over 670 for the first time and comfortably above the 669.57 peak set on Thursday.

Volume on the options exchange soared to 380,000 contracts on Friday, reflecting the monthly options expirations. Dealers said some in the market had been caught out by the New Year rally and were covering bearish index option positions.

Other dealers said new "click fund" options deals done by Dutch securities houses were expiring in favour of holders and writers were also scrambling to cover their exposure, helping turnover to beat the 352,000 daily record set last October.
A click fund offers a secure return linked to gains in the AEX, which many analysts had anticipated would show only modest gains early in 1997 after the surge of 1996.
The AEX began last month at 631, finishing 1996 at 648, after a powerful rise of over 30 percent on 1995, leading analysts to conclude early 1997 could see consolidation.

"I think the gains in the New Year, based on Wall Street and the dollar, have been a bit of a surprise to some," a dealer said. "I don't think anyone really knows what's going to happen next week once the expirations are out of the way."

The index has set five new closing highs since the year began, and is now hovering close to some analysts' targets for the year. The year-end target range of analysts polled last year by Reuters saw the AEX at 578 to 687.
One dealer said that with the approaching Dutch company full year reporting season, trends of strong corporate growth seen so far for 1996 pointed to further strength in the AEX.
"We've got strong fundamentals of good corporate growth, a higher dollar and an outlook for lower inflation. There's no reason the AEX shouldn't go through 700 this year," he said.

Nedlloyd shares spiked up 1.30 guilders to 56.20 on talk of a broker's recommendation, before slipping back to be 20 cents lower at 54.70 guilders. Dealers said the move indicated a fair amount of technical trading related to options.

Philips closed 20 cents easier at 77.20 guilders, back from a 12 month high of 78.20 guilders. Analysts say recent moves such as the winding up of operations at the Superclub home entertainments unit and a move to hold Grundig at arms length show new chairman Cor Boonstra is tackling the firm's problems. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
